differences: The reference dates the Empire to 1804-1806. Our map still labels the whole west of Hispaniola 'Empire of Haiti' in 1809.

Smaller point: our polygon follows the modern Haiti-DR border, including the Central Plateau (Hinche, ~72°W, 19.1°N). The reference marks that area as Spanish territory under French control, 1795-1809.
Related, outside this year: the data also uses 'Empire of Haiti' for 1846-1915, but Soulouque's Second Empire lasted only 1849-1859.

suggested.detail: Divided Haiti: northern State and southern Republic
